sections.title: Form and flowers
sections.text: Red campion is a downy perennial or biennial herb, usually 30–90 cm tall and sometimes near 1 m. Hairy leaves grow in opposite pairs. Male and female flowers occur on separate plants; each flower is about 2–2.5 cm across and has five bright pink petals, deeply notched at the tip.

sections.title: Fruit and look-alike
sections.text: The female flower develops a capsule that opens by recurved teeth. White campion (Silene latifolia) is a close relative with typically white flowers; the two can hybridize. The sources consulted do not establish a safe food use.
